intro: Recorded on 30 September 2026. The agent is Claude, made by Anthropic, connected to four precomputing serve --read-only servers, one for each file above, over HTTP with a read token, through the official MCP TypeScript client (version 2.2.0, protocol 2026-07-28). Claude built this release and had seen these files while building it; in this session it read them only through the tools. The questions were chosen before the first call. Every call, result and answer is shown as it happened, and each note on why a call was made was written with the call.

turns.answer:
/api/report is the endpoint that got slower, and it did so steadily: its p99 went from 584 ms in the 09:00 hour to 620 ms at 10:00 and 659 ms at 11:00, about 13% in three hours, and its average from 275 to 312 ms. Its traffic stayed level at about 54,000 requests an hour and it had no burst of unusual requests, so this is a gradual slowdown, not an incident.

/api/checkout looks worse in the 10:00 hour (p99 907 ms), but that is one short incident: from 10:30 to 10:32 its average rose from about 128 ms to 760 to 770 ms and its p99 to about 1.6 seconds, with 1,111 requests flagged as unusual. By 10:32 it was back to normal, and it ended the three hours near 270 ms, where it started. The other three endpoints held steady. The percentiles come from the file's sketches and are within 1%.

steps.why: One step, at 18:31:05 UTC (14:31:05 in New York), z of -610. One-minute candles from four minutes before to twelve after.
Check the rest of the day by the hour, to be sure no slower move was bigger than the step.

turns.answer:
SIM6's biggest move by far was a single step at 14:31:05 New York time (18:31:05 UTC): the price fell from about 145.2 to 136.48 in one trade, about 6%. The file flagged it as SIM6's only unusual step of the day, with a z-score of -610. Until then SIM6 had traded between 144.04 and 146.32.

In the minutes after, trading jumped. Before the drop it ran at about 750 trades and 250,000 shares a minute; from 14:32 to 14:35 it ran at about 3,000 trades and 920,000 to 990,000 shares a minute, about four times as busy, while the price slid a little further, to 136.06. From 14:36 it calmed to about 1,050 trades a minute, still above its earlier pace, and held between 135.8 and 136.4. By the close at 16:00 it had recovered to 138.08, still about 5% below where it stood before the drop.

turns.answer:
Sundial Research brought the most revenue in September: $2,591.16 due, which is $3,454.87 at list price less its 25% Enterprise discount, for 150,790 requests. Harbor Legal Drafts was close behind at $2,374.67 for 39,586 requests. Quarry Road Media owes $683.48 and Maple Grove Travel $155.25, and the two Free customers owe nothing: $5,804.56 in all.

One customer ran out of quota: Juniper Bakery Blog, on the Free plan, reached its 5,000,000 tokens (5,000,309 were counted; the request that crossed the line still counts). Its daily usage stops on 27 September, with 10 requests that day and none after, which fits the gateway turning it away once the quota was reached. Nobody else came close: Quarry used 57% of its 300 million tokens, Harbor 46%, Northgate 31% of its 5 million and Maple 27%. Sundial, on Enterprise, has no quota.

turns.answer:
Two things changed in that hour.

At 12:40 the payment provider northpay started failing. From 12:40:03 to 12:47:58 its charges came back as errors with status 503: 355 failed charges, while northpay's successful charges fell from 391 in the ten minutes before to 66. The other two providers, quickcard and banklink, carried on as usual. Shoppers felt it: 214 orders failed with reason payment_error between 12:40:01 and 12:47:59, and the web server's /checkout requests slowed from a median of about 160 ms to 460 ms, with a p95 near one second, until about 12:50. After 12:48 northpay's charges went through again.

At 13:05 search started writing a new DEBUG line, ranking batch. It is not an error, but it is loud: search went from about 2,700 lines every ten minutes to about 11,600, four times as many, and the new pattern had written 46,734 lines by 14:00.
